subject: robust predictions on wrong values - does make sense in a bayesan context?

messages.author: 7a97c986864bf6d6
messages.subject: robust predictions on wrong values - does make sense in a bayesan context?
parts:
Hello,

I have almost completed my model, a deconvolution model of mixed gene expression.

 Is predicting quite well, with 99% accuracy for noiseless data.

Now, a strange thing happen. For some genes, it makes prediction on wrong values with a high confidence. The question is: where does it invent this signals from? I understand if it predicts wrong values with high variance if it cant find signal within noise, but...




On y axes reference values, on x predicted. The two plots are identical subsets of the data set that have common prior for each gene (dots) for difference cell types (colors).

Does this behavior (wrong predictions with high confidence) make sense?

Thanks

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] robust predictions on wrong values - does make sense in a bayesan context?
parts:
Hard to say without looking at your model and trying
to verify you didn't make an indexing error somewhere
(often the problem in this kind of thing in my experience).

Wrong predictions with high confidence often arise from
false independence assumptions, as in naive Bayes
classifiers.

- Bob
